title: Easy Cheeseburger Penne Skillet (30-Minute Dinner)
imageAlt: Easy cheeseburger penne skillet with ground beef, tomatoes, melted cheddar, and parsley
contentHtml:
This easy cheeseburger penne skillet turns the flavors of a classic cheeseburger into a hearty one-pan pasta dinner in about 30 minutes. Ground beef, tomatoes, mustard, Worcestershire, cheddar, and tender penne make it familiar enough for kids but satisfying enough for a hungry weeknight crowd.

The pasta cooks right in the skillet, so there is no separate pot to wash. If you are cooking for a different family size, use the Family Meal Planning Tools recipe scaler to adjust the quantities.

Easy Cheeseburger Penne Skillet Recipe

Prep time: 10 minutes
Cook time: 20 minutes
Total time: 30 minutes
Yield: 6 servings

Equipment

  • 12-inch deep skillet or Dutch oven with lid
  • Wooden spoon or silicone spatula
  • Chef's knife and cutting board
  • Measuring cups and spoons
  • Instant-read thermometer

Ingredients

  • 1 tablespoon olive oil
  • 1 pound lean ground beef
  • 1 small yellow onion, diced
  • 3 garlic cloves, minced
  • 2 tablespoons tomato paste
  • 1 tablespoon Worcestershire sauce
  • 1 tablespoon yellow mustard
  • 1 teaspoon smoked paprika
  • 1/2 teaspoon kosher salt
  • 1/4 teaspoon black pepper
  • 1 can diced tomatoes with juices, 14.5 ounces
  • 3 cups low-sodium beef broth
  • 12 ounces dry penne pasta
  • 1/2 cup evaporated milk or whole milk
  • 1 1/2 cups shredded sharp cheddar cheese
  • 1/2 cup shredded mozzarella cheese
  • 2 tablespoons chopped fresh parsley

Numbered Instructions

  1. Brown the beef. Heat the olive oil in a deep skillet over medium-high heat. Add the ground beef and onion. Cook for 6 to 8 minutes, breaking the beef into small crumbles, until no pink remains and the beef reaches 160°F. Drain excess grease if needed.
  2. Season the skillet. Reduce the heat to medium. Stir in the garlic, tomato paste, Worcestershire sauce, mustard, smoked paprika, salt, and black pepper. Cook for 1 minute, stirring constantly.
  3. Add the pasta. Pour in the diced tomatoes and beef broth. Stir in the dry penne and bring the liquid to a gentle boil.
  4. Simmer until tender. Reduce the heat to medium-low, cover, and simmer for 12 to 14 minutes. Stir every 3 to 4 minutes so the pasta does not stick. The penne is ready when it is al dente and most of the liquid has been absorbed.
  5. Make it creamy. Stir in the evaporated milk. Simmer uncovered for 1 to 2 minutes if the sauce looks thin.
  6. Add the cheese. Reduce the heat to low. Stir in 1 cup cheddar and 1/4 cup mozzarella until melted. Sprinkle the remaining cheese over the top, cover for 2 minutes, and let it melt.
  7. Finish and serve. Remove from the heat, sprinkle with parsley, and let the skillet rest for 3 minutes so the sauce thickens slightly before serving.

Doneness and Food-Safety Cues

  • Ground beef should reach 160°F before the remaining ingredients are added.
  • The penne should be tender but still have a slight bite in the center.
  • The finished sauce should coat the pasta instead of pooling heavily at the bottom of the skillet.
  • If the skillet becomes dry before the pasta is tender, add beef broth or water 1/4 cup at a time.

Useful Cooking Tips

  • Use lean beef. An 85/15 or 90/10 blend gives plenty of flavor without leaving the pasta greasy.
  • Stir during the simmer. One-pan pasta needs an occasional stir so the penne cooks evenly and does not stick to the bottom.
  • Shred the cheese yourself when possible. Freshly shredded cheese melts more smoothly than many pre-shredded blends.
  • Let it rest before serving. Three minutes off the heat gives the sauce time to cling to the pasta.

Substitutions

  • Use ground turkey or chicken instead of beef and cook poultry to 165°F.
  • Use rotini or small shells in place of penne; start checking for doneness a few minutes early.
  • Replace mozzarella with additional cheddar for a sharper cheeseburger flavor.
  • Use regular paprika if you do not have smoked paprika.
  • For extra vegetables, cook 1 diced bell pepper with the onion.

Storage and Reheating

Cool leftovers promptly and refrigerate them in an airtight container for up to 4 days. Reheat individual servings in the microwave in 45-second intervals, stirring between intervals. Add 1 tablespoon milk or broth before reheating if the sauce has thickened.

To reheat on the stovetop, warm the pasta in a covered skillet over low heat with a small splash of broth. This dish can be frozen for up to 2 months, although the pasta will be a little softer after thawing.

Frequently Asked Questions

Do I cook the penne before adding it?

No. The dry pasta cooks directly in the beef broth and tomato mixture, which is what makes this a true one-pan dinner.

Can I make this less cheesy?

Yes. Use 1 cup cheddar total and skip the mozzarella. The sauce will be lighter but still creamy from the milk and starch released by the pasta.

What can I serve with cheeseburger pasta?

A simple green salad, roasted broccoli, green beans, or sliced cucumbers keeps the meal balanced without adding much extra work.

Estimated Nutrition

Estimated per serving: about 610 calories, 34 grams protein, 58 grams carbohydrates, 27 grams fat, and 4 grams fiber. Nutrition varies by beef, cheese, broth, milk, and serving size.
